Time Memoria — FFXIV quest progression and pacing. Pre-release rebuild on a generated quest data layer. # Time Memoria

A FFXIV Dalamud plugin for quest progression and pacing — a reflective notebook
for your story journey, not a scoreboard.

> ⚠️ This plugin **cannot** be used for ACT/FFLogs-style performance analysis.
> It does not track, read, or evaluate combat performance in any way.

![The Quests tab](assets/quests.png)

Browse by expansion and section, or let **Recommended** answer "what next" — the
oldest thing outstanding, the next Main Scenario quest, and the next quest for
every job you have actually unlocked. The patch each quest arrived in is not in
the game's own tables; it ships as data.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Overview](assets/overview.png) | ![Progression](assets/progression.png) |
| Completion by expansion and by section. Excluded categories stay visible but uncounted. | Class and job levels, coloured by role, marking the least progressed in each. |

![The at-a-glance window](assets/mini.png)

A small companion window for while you are actually playing: playtime with the
age of the reading, session and lifetime pacing, and the battle jobs furthest
behind.

Every window above is drawn with the game's own widgets. There is a classic
ImGui version of all of it too — `/tm classic` — and a setting for which one
`/tm` opens.

---

## Status: released

**Time Memoria is published.** Install it by adding this repository to Dalamud's
custom plugin repositories:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3/main/repo.json
```

It is also carried by [Senither's plugin
list](https://dalamud-plugins.senither.com/plugin/TimeMemoriaV3), which merges a
number of third-party repositories into a single URL.

Two earlier versions were built and flown before this one, which is why it began
at **3.0** rather than 1.0 — it is shaped by what they taught.

[TimeMemoriaV2](https://github.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV2) is kept for
reference. It maintained its quest data by hand — 288 JSON files needing an
update every patch — and that is why it stalled: patch 7.5 landed in April 2026
and the data was never added.

This version reads quest data from the game's own journal tables instead, so a
patch's content appears the day it lands and no one has to do anything. That is
the whole point of the rebuild, and it is a direct answer to how the last one
failed. Numbering it 1.0 would hide that.

### Module state

| Module | State |
|---|---|
| Quest UI | ✅ generated from journal tables |
| News / Events | ✅ feed plus client-read festivals |
| Playtime & pacing | ✅ session and lifetime |
| Class & job progression | ✅ with clipboard export |
| Patch attribution | ✅ patch column on quests and What's New |
| Native game windows | ✅ every tab, plus a companion window |
| Ocean Fishing helper | ❌ future |

### Versioning

`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.API` — releasing at **`3.0.0.15`**.

The last digit is the Dalamud API level the build targets, so you can tell which
game version a build is for without opening the manifest. It is safe in the last
position: API levels only ever climb, so the version stays monotonic, which
Dalamud requires for updates to install. Putting it *first* would make a routine
API bump look like a major release of the plugin.

Time Memoria v2 used `AA.B.C.D`, where the digits encoded API level, expansion
band, patch band, and how many quest buckets had been hand-extracted. That was
right for a plugin whose central problem was migrating quest data by hand — the
version told you how far through it you were.

This version has no buckets, and covers every expansion and patch the moment the
game does. Under the old scheme it would read `15.7.5.9` on day one and never
move again. The module table above carries what those digits used to.

### What works

- Quest data generated from the game's own journal tables — no hand-maintained
  quest files, so a patch's content appears the day it lands
- Two-panel questline tree, chain-grouped, with search across every expansion
  including ones the tree is hiding
- Suggested next quest, and per-expansion and per-category progress
- The patch each quest arrived in — not in the game files at all, so it ships
  as data
- MSQ progression gating, spoiler mode, free-trial mode
- Class and job levelling, role-coloured, with clipboard export
- Playtime pacing, session and lifetime
- World state: maintenance windows, patch status, and active events read from
  the client rather than only from the news feed
- What's New — quests added since the baseline snapshot, with the build they
  arrived in
- Per-character completion dates from first install onwards
- Help and Credits

---

## Building

Native UI comes from [KamiToolKit](https://github.com/MidoriKami/KamiToolKit),
which is not published as a package — it is a submodule, and **the build will
fail without it**:

```
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3
```

Already cloned? `git submodule update --init --recursive`, then:

```
dotnet build TimeMemoria.csproj
```

Requires the .NET 10 SDK and a Dalamud development environment.

The assembly is named `TimeMemoriaV3` permanently. Dalamud derives InternalName
from it, and InternalName keys the configuration file and the directory holding
the quest journal — renaming it would orphan both. Only the display name matters
to anyone using the plugin, and that is `Time Memoria`.

---

## Credits

Time Memoria's quest data layer derives from **QuestTracker**, originally by
[isaiahcat](https://github.com/isaiahcat/QuestTracker) and currently maintained
by [keifufu](https://github.com/keifufu/QuestTracker), used under AGPL-3.0. It
is an independent plugin, not affiliated with or endorsed by either author.

See [NOTICE](NOTICE) for the full attribution and the list of changes.

Inspiration, though no code, also came from
[BetterPlaytime](https://github.com/caitlyn-gg/BetterPlaytime) by Infi and
Caitlyn, and [LeveHelper](https://github.com/Haselnussbomber/LeveHelper) by
Haselnussbomber.

---

## Compliance

Time Memoria is strictly a quest progression and pacing tool.

It does **not**:

- Read or display DPS, HPS, deaths, wipes, or duty results
- Integrate with ACT, FFLogs, or any combat log format
- Automate any in-game interaction
- Transmit your data anywhere — the clipboard export is local and user-initiated

Saved data is limited to quest IDs, completion counts, timestamps, pacing
aggregates, and class/job levels. Nothing it stores can be repurposed as a
combat log.

---

## AI usage

Development was AI-assisted at the **Copilot** level as defined by Dalamud's
[AI Usage Policy](https://dalamud.dev/plugin-publishing/ai-policy/) — AI
implements, the maintainer plans, tests and reviews. No assets are AI-generated.

[AI-DECLARATION.md](AI-DECLARATION.md) records this in full, including what AI
got wrong and how it was caught.

---

## Licence

[AGPL-3.0](LICENSE).

variant.changelog:
Our largest update since 3.0.

Native window - Story Remaining:
- Add Story Remaining to the Native overview. It existed only in Classic, so switching to the window being actively developed cost you the projection that most justifies the plugin.
- Reproduce Classic's wording exactly, down to the singular "quest" when one is left and the gate sentence being dropped on the final expansion.
- Move the calculation out of Classic's draw code into a shared helper both windows now call, so the two can no longer drift apart or disagree on a figure.
- Quote a single pacing figure. Story Remaining previously cited the Main Scenario rate three rows under a row showing the same number, so "28m per quest" could sit above "at your rate of 28m 16s per quest".
- Make the overview panel scroll, and raise its capacity from 26 rows to 48. At the 460px minimum window size the surplus rows did not vanish - they drew over the window's own border.
- Hide a row's whole container rather than just its text, so the scrollbar describes the rows you can actually see instead of counting hidden ones.
- Say so, once, if the row pool is ever exhausted. Silently dropping the surplus is why the old ceiling went unnoticed for as long as it did.

Native window - News and Bonuses:
- Merge News and What's New into one "News/What's New" tab, News taking the upper 60%. Both panels are unchanged; they are composed rather than rewritten.
- Add a Bonuses tab showing your fed status and the current food recommendation. The information was already read live, but the full window never had access to it - only the companion window did.
- List every food you are holding, grouped into Combat, Crafting and Gathering by which stats the item actually grants, rather than guessed from its name.
- Rank food within each group using the same cap-first scoring already used to choose the single recommendation, so the tab and the recommendation cannot contradict each other.
- List NQ and HQ of the same item as separate rows, since their bonuses differ, and highlight only the row for the quality you are actually holding.

Recommendations:
- Offer the ten oldest unfinished quests instead of one. The pane it opens into already scrolled and already held a dozen job quests, so nothing new was needed to show them.
- Keep the single quest Classic names unchanged. Ten entries meant deciding what happens when two quests tie on both patch and level; the new ordering was checked against the old one over 20,000 generated cases built to collide often, and the top entry matched every time.
- Cost nothing extra on a new character. The list is built by bounded insertion rather than sorting - on a character with almost nothing complete, sorting five thousand quests to keep ten would throw away 99.8% of the work.
- Add a setting to leave class and job quests out of the shortlist, on by default. Every A Realm Reborn class has an unlock quest at level 1 in patch 2.0, so they tie on both sort keys and could fill all ten slots on a character who has not taken them all.
- Offer it as a setting rather than a filter, because they genuinely are the oldest outstanding quests. Someone working through the classes wants them listed; someone who never intends to wants that corner of the backlog out of the way.
- Match those quests by their English titles, the same method the totals and the export already use, so the setting behaves identically on every client language rather than silently doing nothing.
- Leave the tree, the totals and the export untouched. The setting says what to recommend, not what your character has done.
- Apply the setting immediately. It previously recomputed the shortlist while the screen showed the old one, and only corrected itself when you closed and reopened the window.
- Preserve your scroll position when nothing relevant changed. The list rebuilds when the setting has moved, not on every visit to the tab.
- Hide Recommended entirely under the Done filter. Every quest in it is unfinished by definition, so each branch opened onto blankness rather than saying nothing matched.

Achievement counts:
- Show collectables and duty counts without requiring you to open one specific achievement page first. These came from a single slot holding whichever achievement the client last fetched, so for most characters the three counts simply stayed blank.
- Read them instead from which achievement tiers you have completed, which is available all at once and needs no request to the server.
- Present the result as a guaranteed floor rather than a running total. A completed tier proves you reached its requirement; it cannot tell you how far past it you are.
- Take the reading once per session, since a completed tier cannot become uncompleted.
- Recover the requirement from each achievement's description, because no column in the game's own data holds it.
- Discard an entire achievement series if its parsed requirements do not increase with its tiers. A reworded tier or an unfamiliar language shows up as nonsense ordering, and no figure at all is better than a wrong one presented as a guarantee.
- Name the specific achievement to open in the companion window's hint. The old wording said to open Achievements once, which was wrong - the window can be open and still show nothing.

Adventurer's Ledger export:
- Add thirteen unlock keys the ledger had been approximating from your story patch: a daily key and an elite key for each of the five Hunt boards, plus allied societies, Zodiac and raids.
- Treat the Hunt as five features rather than one. Each expansion has its own board, its own unlock chain and its own weekly elite bill.
- Include Zodiac, previously left out because "A Relic Reborn" is per weapon. The ledger's row is Morbid Motivation, and all thirteen weapon quests converge well before it, so a single quest answers it.
- Keep the existing "eliteHunt" name even though it has always meant the Heavensward chain specifically. Published builds already send it and its value has not changed - only which ledger row should read it was wrong.

Notes:
- New settings arrive with defaults; nothing needs configuring after updating.
- Per-item bag and slot location for food was built and then dropped. The bag reads back correctly, but the inventory window's layout is a client display setting that plugins cannot see, so any "row 3, slot 5" would have been wrong for some players and right for others with no way to tell which.

Something not working, or a figure that looks wrong? Please reach out.

variant.changelog:
Native window improvements: a cleaner News tab, an at-a-glance achievement total, and role-coloured, correctly-ranked food.

News and What's New:
- Merge What's New into the News tab. It was dormant between content patches and had one line to say the rest of the year while permanently holding 40% of the tab's height for it - now it's one continuous panel that only grows a list when there is something to list.
- List up to 60 new quests on a big patch, and say so ("...and N more") rather than silently dropping the rest.

Overview:
- Add an "Achievements" section - "Overall X/Y Z%" - the same grand tally the game's own Achievements window shows, in both Classic and Native.
- Hidden until that window has loaded this login, the same way other totals hide rather than showing a false 0/0.
- Fixes a related gap: switching characters mid-session could silently skip this and other free achievement reads for every character after the first.

Bonuses:
- Colour each held food's stat line by role - Tank, Healer, DPS, Crafter, Gatherer - matching the palette Progression already uses.
- Fix a ranking bug: food was scored by summing every stat's cap regardless of relevance, so a Skill Speed/Direct Hit food could outrank a Piety food for a healer. Ranking now counts only the stats your equipped gear actually uses.
- Rank held food by your real, current stat totals while you are not fed, instead of assuming every food reaches its cap; falls back to the simpler cap-based ranking while fed, since your current total already includes that food's own bonus and multiplying it in again would double-count it.
- Pin the food you are currently eating to the top of its group.

Something not working, or a figure that looks wrong? Please reach out.
